title: Describe a structured search carried by HTTP QUERY
goal: Map a read-only search body with HTTP QUERY and choose its native OpenAPI 3.2 operation or earlier-version extension after checking client support.

selectionNotes: HTTP QUERY needs end-to-end method/body support. OpenAPI 3.2 uses query; 3.0/3.1 use x-oai-additionalOperations. A generator may ignore the extension. RFC 10008 supersedes the draft named by older release notes.

constraints: HTTP QUERY needs end-to-end method/body support. OpenAPI 3.2 uses query; 3.0/3.1 use x-oai-additionalOperations. A generator may ignore the extension. RFC 10008 supersedes the draft named by older release notes.

The inventory/release notes call QUERY a proposal; the linked IETF draft now resolves to the June 2026 Proposed Standard RFC 10008. That source correction does not establish universal adoption. Test method allowlists, browser CORS/preflight, gateways, caches and client generators in your deployment; the sample proves HttpClient to loopback Kestrel only. An extension can be retained by a parser and still be ignored by a generator. Request bodies do not remove size limits or supply validation/access control. Caching and automatic retries require the real method semantics and appropriate implementation; no cache or intermediary behavior is demonstrated.
stabilityLimitations: Stable framework capability, prepared with .NET 11 RC2 artifacts under ADR 0004. GA source/package/runtime reconciliation remains separate.
